name: Tactical Pause
description: Owns whether a continuous-time encounter is advancing or paused, and why. Manual pause and configurable auto-pause are edges into that one state, not separate pause systems. It never rolls initiative, emits turns, advances cooldowns, queues orders, or resolves combat: combat.turn_order_queue remains the discrete-turn owner, combat.party_command_queue holds intentions, and the ordinary combat components resolve released actions. Auto-pause emits only on a running-to-paused transition so repeated damage or status events cannot produce a pause storm.

inputs.name: allowManualPause
inputs.description: Whether input.pause may toggle the simulation clock. When false, only configured automatic reasons may pause.

inputs.name: autoPauseOnEnemySpotted
inputs.description: Pause when combat.aggroGained reports a new hostile engagement.

inputs.name: autoPauseOnPartyMemberDefeated
inputs.description: Pause when a living party member is defeated; unrelated enemy defeats do not trigger this reason.

inputs.name: autoPauseOnEffectApplied
inputs.description: Pause on combat.effectApplied. Off by default because routine damage-over-time refreshes would make combat unreadably stop-start.

outputs.name: paused
outputs.description: The authoritative pause state consumed by the simulation scheduler.

outputs.name: pauseReason
outputs.description: manual | enemySpotted | partyMemberDefeated | effectApplied, or null while running.

outputs.name: simulationTimeScale
outputs.description: 0 while paused and 1 while running; presentation time is deliberately not owned here.

provenance: BG2-inspired extraction pass on 2026-11-02 searched turn_order_queue, round_manager, game_speed, beat_clock, timer_system and aggro_table. The turn queue pauses for discrete initiative turns, game_speed changes rate rather than tactical state, timers execute scheduled work, and aggro owns detection only. No contract owned continuous-time pause policy or one-shot auto-pause reasons, so this adds that boundary without changing turn-based behavior.
